key_facts.fact_en: The accident happened on 16 Jun 2026, after 1 Jun 2026, so the new Civil Transactions Law (Federal Decree-Law No. 25 of 2025) governs the claim, not the 1985 law

The criminal judgment of 28 Jul 2026 (case 3471/2026, traffic misdemeanours) convicted the first defendant and fined him AED 10,000; it became final without appeal (court certificate of 3 Sep 2026), and the claim relies on it under Evidence Law Article 88
The police report puts 100% of the responsibility on the first defendant, who ran a red light, as shown by the junction camera and an eyewitness
Injuries: comminuted fracture of the right tibia and fibula and a fracture of the right ankle; surgery on 17 Jun 2026; in hospital until 29 Jun 2026; 36 physiotherapy sessions
Permanent partial disability of the right lower limb: 15%, written by hand by the treating doctor on the final medical report; the claim states the same figure
Sick leave from 16 Jun to 15 Oct 2026; fit to return to work from 16 Oct 2026, avoiding long periods of standing

reader_should_flag: The quotation of Article 255 of the Civil Transactions Law (Federal Decree-Law No. 25 of 2025) does not match the official text: it says 'نتيجة محتملة' (a probable consequence), but the official word is 'طبيعية' ('نتيجة طبيعية للفعل الضار', a natural consequence of the harmful act). The changed word widens the damage the claim says can be recovered.
The accident (16 Jun 2026) is after 1 Jun 2026, so the 2025 Civil Transactions Law applies; the 1985 law's article numbers (282, 292, 293) must not be used.
The permanent disability percentage (15%) on the medical report is handwritten by the doctor.
The filing date (26 Oct 2026) appears only in the registry stamp; the claim itself is dated 22 Oct 2026.
The AED 10,000 in the facts is the criminal fine, not a compensation item.
